item.title: Legoland Japan and the Minato Area: Nagoya's Family Playground — Guide
item.description: Legoland Japan opened in Nagoya’s redeveloped Kinjofuto port district as the country’s only Legoland resort, its seven themed zones built from some 10 million bricks and pitched squarely at families with children aged roughly two to twelve. The park’s showpiece is Miniland, where Japanese landmarks from Tokyo Tower to Nagoya Castle are rebuilt in astonishing brick detail, and the surrounding Minato area rounds out a family day with the Sea Life aquarium, the Maker’s Pier shopping village and the neighbouring SCMaglev railway museum.

item.title: Toyama Family Travel Guide: Tateyama Alpine Route, Kurobe Dam & Firefly Squid
item.description: Toyama is one of Japan’s best family destinations for families who want more than temples and shopping. The prefecture offers a scale of natural and engineering spectacle that genuinely impresses children — snow walls higher than apartment buildings, a dam with a water cannon, and a sea that produces bioluminescent light. Most of the major experiences are accessible on public transport with children in tow. Alpine Route for Families The Tateyama Kurobe Alpine Route works particularly well for children because the journey itself is the entertainment.

item.title: Shiga with Kids: Ninja Village, Castle Cat & Lake Biwa Cruises
item.description: Shiga Prefecture sits an eight-minute train ride from Kyoto, but it operates at an entirely different pace. Here, Japan’s largest lake spreads across the landscape like an inland sea, a real castle still stands on the hill where it was built four centuries ago, and children can throw shuriken at a village where the techniques of historical ninja have been preserved and taught for generations. For families travelling Japan, this is a prefecture that repays a full day or two without requiring a car.
